entries.principle_source: OECD Recommendation of the Council on Artificial Intelligence, OECD/LEGAL/0449 (2019, revised 2024), principle 1.4; a non-binding OECD Recommendation
entries.instrument: Law of the Republic of Kazakhstan 'On Artificial Intelligence' No. 230-VIII of 17 November 2025
entries.provision: Art. 11(1) (AI systems must meet safety and reliability requirements excluding unforeseen consequences or abuse); Art. 15(2)(2) (owners must ensure safety and reliability, incl. protection against failures)
entries.why_here: In Part 4 the bare pipeline decided on GPA 9.9 and exam -5 (reject) instead of stopping; validation refused it with invalid_input and 0 model calls, and refused none of the 400 clean applicants.

entries.principle_source: UNESCO Recommendation on the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence (2021), paras. 28-30; non-binding, applied by Member States on a voluntary basis (para. 2)
entries.instrument: Constitution of the Republic of Kazakhstan (adopted by referendum 15 March 2026); Law 'On Artificial Intelligence' No. 230-VIII of 17.11.2025; Law 'On Personal Data and Their Protection' No. 94-V of 21.05.2013
entries.provision: Constitution Art. 16(2) (no discrimination by origin, sex, language, place of residence or any other circumstance); AI Law Art. 6 (AI must exclude any such discrimination); Law 94-V Art. 7(9) (data excessive to the purpose must not be processed)
entries.why_here: Part 1 measured a systematic score advantage for flagship over identical regional applicants (+2.5 [+1.1, +4.1] points, sign p = 0.002) and 4 gender flips all favouring female names (p = 0.125, not established); name and university are not fund criteria, so the model no longer sees them.

entries.principle_source: UNESCO Recommendation on the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence (2021), paras. 25-26; non-binding
entries.instrument: Law of the Republic of Kazakhstan 'On Personal Data and Their Protection' No. 94-V of 21 May 2013 (as amended by Law No. 231-VIII of 17.11.2025); Law 'On Artificial Intelligence' No. 230-VIII
entries.provision: Law 94-V Art. 19-1(1) (automated processing that creates, changes or ends rights only with consent), Art. 7(1) (consent of the subject or legal representative), Art. 7(8) (processing limited to predetermined purposes); AI Law Art. 11(1) (no abuse of AI systems)
entries.why_here: In Part 4 the bare pipeline screened all 6 requests and turned a missing consent and an age of 17 into rejections and a ranking-by-ethnicity request into a shortlist; the harness refused 5 of 6 with 0 model calls and 0 wrong refusals among 400 clean applicants.

entries.principle_source: UNESCO Recommendation on the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence (2021), paras. 42-43; OECD/LEGAL/0449, principle 1.5 (Accountability); both non-binding
entries.instrument: Law of the Republic of Kazakhstan 'On Artificial Intelligence' No. 230-VIII of 17 November 2025; benchmark only: EU AI Act, Regulation (EU) 2024/1689
entries.provision: AI Law Art. 8(1)-(2) (constant control over the AI system; responsibility for its results), Art. 15(2)(3) (owners must keep documentation on the AI system); benchmark: AI Act Art. 12(1) (automatic logs) and Art. 26(6) (keep logs at least six months)
entries.why_here: Blinding changed 166 of 400 scores (mean 14.01 points) and 63 of 400 outcomes, so without a per-decision record of what the model was shown and which rule acted, nobody could later tell why an applicant got their outcome.

entries.principle_source: UNESCO Recommendation on the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence (2021), paras. 35-36; non-binding
entries.instrument: Law of the Republic of Kazakhstan 'On Personal Data and Their Protection' No. 94-V of 21 May 2013; Law 'On Artificial Intelligence' No. 230-VIII of 17.11.2025
entries.provision: Law 94-V Art. 19-1(2)-(3) (explain automated processing, allow an objection, consider it within three working days); AI Law Art. 7(2) (right to be informed and to object), Art. 9 (human autonomy in decision-making)
entries.why_here: In Part 1 the model gave both decisions at score 45 and all 4 gender flips sat at this boundary; the harness sends every reject and the band (40, 45) to a person: 58 of 400 (14.5%) against 64 of 400 (16.0%) planned, and 0 automatic rejects.
